```{r message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
# Import modules
library(posterior)
library(bayesplot)
library(ggplot2)

# Import functions
library(cmdstanr)

# Create ./stan folder if does not exists
if (!dir.exists("./stan")) {
    dir.create("./stan")
}
```

```{r}
df <- read.csv("grouse_data.csv", row.names = 1)
head(df)
```

```{r}
hist(df$TICKS, breaks = 20, main = 'Number of ticks', col = 'lightblue')
```

Let $y_i$ number of ticks on a grouse. As covariates we consider $x_i = [1, h_i]$ where $h_i$ is the height of the place where the grouse lives.

As standard practice we standardize the covariates

The model assumes

$$
    \begin{aligned}
        y_i \mid \beta & \sim \text{Poi}(\exp(x_i^T \, \beta))\\
        \beta_j \mid \sigma_j & \sim \mathcal{N}(0, \sigma_j^2) \\
        \sigma_j &\sim \mathcal{HC}(0, 1)
    \end{aligned}
$$

Where $\mathcal{HC}(0, 1)$ is the half-Cauchy distribution (i.e. Cauchy truncated on $[0, +\infty)$ centered in $0$ and with scale $1$.

```{r}
y <- df$TICKS
h <- df$HEIGHT
h <- (h - mean(h)) / sd(h)

X <- cbind(1, h)
X[1:10, ]
```

```{r message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
poi_glm <- "
data {
    int<lower=0> N; 
    int<lower=0> p;
    array[N] int<lower=0> Y;
    matrix[N, p] X;
}

parameters {
    vector[p] beta;        
    vector<lower=0>[p] sigma_beta;
}


transformed parameters {
    vector[N] mu;
    for(i in 1:N) {
      mu[i] = exp(row(X, i) * beta);
    }
}

model {   
    for (s in 1:N) {
        Y[s] ~ poisson(mu[s]);  
    }
    

    for (j in 1:p) {
        beta[j] ~ normal(0.0, sigma_beta[j]);
        sigma_beta[j] ~ cauchy(0.0, 1.0);
    }
}

generated quantities {
  vector[N] log_lik;
  for (j in 1:N) {
    log_lik[j] = poisson_lpmf(Y[j] | mu[j]);
  }
}
"

# Write stan model to file
stan_file <- "./stan/poisson_glm.stan"
writeLines(poi_glm, stan_file)

# Compile stan model
poi_glm <- cmdstan_model(stan_file)
```

```{r}
# Input data
glm_data <- list(
    N = length(y),
    p = ncol(X),
    Y = y,
    X = X
)

# Sample
poi_glm_fit <- poi_glm$sample(
    data = glm_data,
    chains = 4,
    parallel_chains = 4,
    iter_warmup = 1000,
    iter_sampling = 5000,
    refresh = 2000
)

poi_glm_data <- posterior::as_draws(poi_glm_fit)
```

```{r}
mcmc_trace(poi_glm_data, pars = c("beta[1]", "beta[2]", "sigma_beta[1]", "sigma_beta[2]"))
```

```{r}
sum(poi_glm_fit$sampler_diagnostics()[, , "divergent__"])
```

# Incorporating additional information in the model

We have that data are divided by years (95, 96, 97).

How can we take this into account?

Of course adding the year as a linear predictor makes very little sense

## Mixed models

We consider that there is a "random effect" specific for each year:

$$
\begin{aligned}
        y_{i,t} \mid  \mu_{i, t} & \sim \text{Poi}(\mu_{i, t}) \\
        \mu_{i, t} & = \exp \left(x_i^T \beta + \lambda_t \right) \\
        \beta_j \mid \sigma_j & \sim \mathcal{N}(0, \sigma_j^2) \\
        \sigma_j &\sim \mathcal{HC}(0, 1) \\
        \lambda_1, \ldots, \lambda_T \mid \lambda_0, s_0 & \sim \mathcal{N}(\lambda_0, s_0)\\
        \lambda_0, s_0 & \sim \mathcal{N}(\lambda_{00}, \tau_0) \times \mathcal{HC}(0, 1)
    \end{aligned}
$$

Where $y_{i, t}$ makes the dependence on the year explicit ($t$).

Here $\lambda_t$ is a random intercept specific of the year

A more convenient formulation is

$$
\begin{aligned}
        y_{i} \mid \mu_i & \sim \text{Poi}(\mu_{i})\\
        \mu_{i} & = \exp \left(x_i^T \beta + g_i^T \lambda \right) \\
        \beta_j \mid \sigma_j & \sim \mathcal{N}(0, \sigma_j^2) \\
        \sigma_j &\sim \mathcal{HC}(0, 1) \\
        \lambda_1, \ldots, \lambda_T \mid \lambda_0, s_0 & \sim \mathcal{N}(\lambda_0, s_0)\\
        \lambda_0, s_0 & \sim \mathcal{N}(\lambda_{00}, \tau_0) \times \mathcal{HN}(0, 3)
    \end{aligned}
$$

where $\lambda = (\lambda_1, \lambda_2, \lambda_3)^T$ and $g_i$ is an indicator vector (i.e. $g_i[h] = 1$ iff observation $i$ belongs to group $h$)

We fix $\lambda_{00} = 0$, $\tau_{0} = 3$.

```{r message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
poi_glmm_grouse <- "
data {
    int<lower = 0> N;
    int<lower = 0> p_fix;
    int<lower = 0> n_groups;
    
    array[N] int<lower=0> Y;
    matrix[N, p_fix] X;
    matrix[N, n_groups] G;
}

parameters {
    vector[p_fix] beta;    
    vector<lower=0>[p_fix] sigma_beta;
    
    vector[n_groups] lambda_raw;
    real lambda0;
    real<lower=0> s0;
}

transformed parameters  {
    vector[n_groups] lambda;
    vector[N] mu;
    
    lambda = lambda0 + lambda_raw * s0;
    
    mu = exp(X * beta + G * lambda);
}

model {
    for (s in 1:N) {
        Y[s] ~ poisson(mu[s]);  
    } 

    for (j in 1:p_fix) {
        beta[j] ~ normal(0.0, sigma_beta[j]);
        sigma_beta[j] ~ cauchy(0.0, 1.0);
    }
    
    lambda_raw ~ normal(0.0, 1.0);
    lambda0 ~ normal(0.0, 3.0);
    s0 ~ cauchy(0.0, 3.0);
}

generated quantities  {
    vector[N] log_lik;
    for (j in 1:N) {
        log_lik[j] = poisson_lpmf(Y[j] | mu[j]);
    }
}
"

stan_file <- "./stan/poi_glmm_grouse.stan"
writeLines(poi_glmm_grouse, stan_file)

poi_glmm <- cmdstan_model(stan_file)
```

```{r}
years <- df$YEAR
G <- outer(years, unique(years), "==") * 1
```


```{r}

    N = length(y),
    p_fix = ncol(X),
    n_groups = ncol(G),
    Y = y,
    X = X,
    G = G
)

poi_glmm_fit <- poi_glmm$sample(
    data = glmm_data,
    chains = 4,
    parallel_chains = 4,
    iter_warmup = 1000,
    iter_sampling = 1000,
    refresh = 500
)

poi_glmm_data <- posterior::as_draws(poi_glmm_fit)
```


### Oh no, some divergent iterations! Let's try and increase `adapt_delta` and/or the `max_treedepth`.
Recall that adapt_delta makes more flexible the number of burn-in iterations. max_treedepth refers to a parameter
of the leapfrog integrator.

```{r}
poi_glmm_fit <- poi_glmm$sample(
    data = glmm_data,
    chains = 4,
    parallel_chains = 4,
    adapt_delta = 0.99,
    max_treedepth = 15,
    refresh = 500,
    seed = 345
)
poi_glmm_data <- posterior::as_draws(poi_glmm_fit)
```

```{r}
poi_glmm_fit
```

```{r}
mcmc_trace(poi_glmm_data, pars = c("beta[1]", "lambda[1]", "lambda[2]", "sigma_beta[1]", "lambda0"))
```

```{r}
sum(poi_glmm_fit$sampler_diagnostics()[, , "divergent__"])
```

## Which model achieves the best fit? - WAIC and PSIS-LOO-CV

Both definitions of *WAIC* and *PSIS-LOO-CV* comes from [Vehtari et al. (2016)](https://link.springer.com/article/10.1007/s11222-016-9696-4).

```{r, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
library(loo)
```


```{r message=TRUE, warning=FALSE}
# Compute and print GLM WAIC
log_lik_glm <- poi_glm_fit$draws("log_lik")
print(waic(log_lik_glm))

# Compute and print GLMM WAIC
log_lik_glmm <- poi_glmm_fit$draws("log_lik")
print(waic(log_lik_glmm))
```

```{r}
print(loo(log_lik_glm))

print(loo(log_lik_glmm))
```


# What is the predictive distribution?

$\newcommand{\iid}{\stackrel{\scriptsize\text{iid}}{\sim}}$ Suppose we have a new covariate $x^*$, what is the distribution of the associated $y^*$?

1.  For the GLM:

$$
    \begin{aligned}
        y_i \mid \beta & \overset{iid}{\sim} \text{Poi}(\exp(x_i^T \, \beta))\\
        \beta_j \mid \sigma_j & \sim \mathcal{N}(0, \sigma_j^2) \\
        \sigma_j &\sim \mathcal{HC}(0, 1)
    \end{aligned}
$$

$$
\begin{aligned}
        \mathcal{L}(y^* \mid \mathbf{y}) &= \int \mathcal{L}(y^* \mid \beta, \mathbf{y}) \mathcal{L}(\beta \mid \mathbf{y}) \mathrm d \beta \\
        & \approx \frac{1}{M} \sum_{j=1}^M \text{Poi}(\exp(x^* \, \beta^{(j)})
    \end{aligned}
$$

2.  For the GLMM, when the observation belongs to one of the observed groups

$$
\begin{aligned}
        y_{i,t} \mid  \lambda_t, \beta & \sim \text{Poi}(\exp \left(x_i^T \beta + \lambda_t \right))\\
        \beta_j \mid \sigma_j & \sim \mathcal{N}(0, \sigma_j^2) \\
        \sigma_j &\sim \mathcal{HC}(0, 1) \\
        \lambda_1, \ldots, \lambda_T \mid \lambda_0, s_0 & \sim \mathcal{N}(\lambda_0, s_0)\\
        \lambda_0, s_0 & \sim \mathcal{N}(\lambda_{00}, \tau_0) \times \mathcal{HN}(0, 3)
    \end{aligned}
$$

$$
\begin{aligned}
        \mathcal{L}(y^* \mid \mathbf{y}) &= \int \mathcal{L}(y^* \mid \lambda_t, \beta, \mathbf{y}) \mathcal{L}(\lambda_t, \beta \mid \mathbf{y}) \mathrm d \beta \\
        & \approx \frac{1}{M} \sum_{j=1}^M \text{Poi}(\exp \left(x^* \beta^{(j)} + \lambda_t^{(j)} \right))
    \end{aligned}
$$

3.  For the GLMM, when the observation belongs to a new group! We need to consider also the law of $\lambda^*$

$$
\begin{aligned}
        \mathcal{L}(y^* , \lambda^* \mid \mathbf{y}) &= \int \mathcal{L}(y^*, \lambda^* \mid \beta, \{\lambda_j\}, \lambda_0, s_0, \mathbf{y}) \mathcal{L}(d \beta, \{d \lambda_j\}, d \lambda_0, d s_0 \mid \mathbf y) \\
        &= \int \mathcal{L}(y^* \mid \lambda^*, \beta) \mathcal{L}(\lambda^* \mid \beta, \{\lambda_j\}, \lambda_{0}, s_0, \mathbf{y}) \mathcal{L}(d \beta, \{d \lambda_j\}, d \lambda_0, d s_0 \mid \mathbf y) \\
        &= \int \mathcal{L}(y^* \mid \lambda_t, \beta) \mathcal{L}(\lambda_t \mid \lambda_{0}, s_0) \mathcal{L}(d \beta, \{d \lambda_j\}, d \lambda_0, d s_0 \mid \mathbf y) \\
    \end{aligned}
$$

So that 

$$
     \mathcal{L}(y^* , \lambda^* \mid \mathbf{y}) = \int \mathcal{L}(y^*, \lambda^* \mid \mathbf{y}) d \lambda^*
$$

We can approximate this integral with

$$
\frac{1}{M} \sum_{j=1}^M \text{Poi}(\exp \left(x^* \beta^{(j)} + \lambda^{*(j)} \right))
$$ 

where $\beta^{(j)}$ is the draw from the MCMC chain and $\lambda^{*(j)} \sim \mathcal{N}(\lambda_0^{(j)}, s_0^{(j)} )$

```{r}
# All of these quantities can be computed either in stan 
# (generated quantities block)
# or directly in R

predictive_poi_glm <- function(x_star, fit, ygrid) {
    betas <- as.matrix(fit$draws("beta", format = "matrix"))
    means <- exp(betas %*% x_star)
    out <- rowMeans(outer(ygrid, as.vector(means), dpois))
    return(out)
}

```

```{r}
predictive_poi_glmm <- function(x_star, group, fit, ygrid) {
    betas <- as.matrix(fit$draws("beta", format = "matrix"))
    lambdas <- as.matrix(fit$draws("lambda", format = "matrix"))
    means <- exp(betas %*% x_star + lambdas[, group])
    out <- rowMeans(outer(ygrid, as.vector(means), dpois))
    return(out)
}
```

```{r}
predictive_poi_glmm_newgroup <- function(x_star, fit, ygrid) {
    # Evaluates P(y=k | x^*, chains) for k in ygrid
    betas <- as.matrix(fit$draws("beta", format = "matrix"))
    lambda0 <- as.vector(fit$draws("lambda0", format = "matrix"))
    s0 <- as.vector(fit$draws("s0", format = "matrix"))
    lambdas <- rnorm(length(lambda0), mean = lambda0, sd = s0)
    means <- exp(betas %*% x_star + lambdas)
    out <- rowMeans(outer(ygrid, as.vector(means), dpois))
    return(out)
}
```

```{r}
x_star <- c(1.0, 0.5)
ygrid <- 0:14

```

```{r}
par(mfrow = c(2, 2))

pred <- predictive_poi_glm(x_star, poi_glm_fit, ygrid)
barplot(pred, names.arg = ygrid, main = "glm", col = 'lightblue')

pred <- predictive_poi_glmm(c(x_star[2]), 1, poi_glmm_fit, ygrid)
barplot(pred, names.arg = ygrid, main = sprintf("glmm, group: %d", 1), col = 'lightblue')

pred <- predictive_poi_glmm(c(x_star[2]), 2, poi_glmm_fit, ygrid)
barplot(pred, names.arg = ygrid, main = sprintf("glmm, group: %d", 3), col = 'lightblue')

pred <- predictive_poi_glmm_newgroup(c(x_star[2]), poi_glmm_fit, ygrid)
barplot(pred, names.arg = ygrid, main = sprintf("glmm, group: %s", "new"), col = 'lightblue')

par(mfrow = c(1, 1))
```

# A more challenging example: the Ant abundance dataset

The dataset contains 60 observations: each observation measures the number of ants found on a tree.\
For each tree we observe/know:

1.  Trap days: how many days the tree was surveyed
2.  Elevation: High (1) or Low (2)
3.  Valley: three different valleys for each elevation --\> nested within the elevation!
4.  Number of ants

Moreover we know:

-   the summer precipitation (avg)
-   the summer temperature (avg)

Let $y_{i, j, r}$ the number of ants observed on tree $i$, at elevation $j$ and valley $r$.\
We assume:

$$
\begin{aligned}
    y_{i, j, r} & \sim \text{Poi}(\mu_{i, j, r}) \\
    \mu_{i, j, r} &= \exp(\theta_j + \alpha_{j, r} + \beta^T x_i + \gamma_j^T z_{i, j} )
\end{aligned}
$$

Some terminology:

-   $\theta_j$ is a random intercept $\to$ group (elevation) specific;
-   $\alpha_{j, r}$ is another random intercept $\to$ group (elevation) AND subgroup (valley) specific;
-   $x_i$ form the fixed effect design matrix, $\beta$ are the fixed regression coefficients;
-   $z_{ij}$ form the RANDOM effect design matrix, $\gamma_j$ are the random effect regression coefficients.

In our case $x_i =$ "trap days", $z_{ij} = (z_{ij1}, z_{ij2})$ = (average precipitation, average temperature).

```{r message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
poi_glm_rand_eff <- "
data{
    int<lower = 0> N;
    int<lower = 0> ngr;
    int<lower = 0> nsubgr;
    
    int<lower = 0> p_fix;
    int<lower = 0> p_ran;
    
    array[N] int<lower = 0> Y;
    matrix[N, p_fix] X;
    matrix[N, p_ran] Z;
    
    array[N] int<lower=1, upper=ngr> group;
    array[N] int<lower=1, upper=nsubgr> subgroup;
}

parameters{
    vector[p_fix] beta;            // regression coefficients (fixed)
    vector[ngr] theta;             // (group specific) random intercept
    matrix[ngr, p_ran] gamma;      // regression coefficients (random)
    vector[nsubgr] alpha;          // (group specific) random effects
    
    vector<lower=0>[p_fix] sigma_beta;        // variances for the prior on beta
    vector<lower=0>[ngr] sigma_theta;         // variances for the prior on theta
    matrix<lower=0>[ngr, p_ran] sigma_gamma;  // (group specific) random effects
    vector<lower=0>[nsubgr] sigma_alpha;      // (group specific) random effects
}

transformed parameters{
    vector[N] mu;
    vector[N] intercept;
    vector[N] fix_eff;
    vector[N] rand_eff;
    
    intercept = theta[group] + alpha[subgroup];    
    fix_eff = X * beta;
    for (i in 1:N) {
        rand_eff[i] = dot_product(Z[i], gamma[group[i]]);
    }
    
    mu = exp(intercept + fix_eff + rand_eff);
}

model{
    for (s in 1:N) {
        Y[s] ~ poisson(mu[s]);  
    } 

    for (j in 1:p_fix) {
        beta[j] ~ normal(0.0, sigma_beta[j]);
        sigma_beta[j] ~ cauchy(0, 1);
    }
    
    for (j in 1:ngr) {
        theta[j] ~ normal(0.0, sigma_theta[j]);
        sigma_theta[j] ~ cauchy(0, 1);
    }
    
    for (j in 1:nsubgr){
        alpha[j] ~ normal(0.0, sigma_alpha);
        sigma_alpha[j] ~ cauchy(0, 1);
    }
    
    for (j in 1:p_ran) {
      for(i in 1:ngr){
        gamma[j,i] ~ normal(0.0, sigma_gamma[j,i]);
        sigma_gamma[j,i] ~ cauchy(0, 1);
      }
    }

}

generated quantities {
     vector[N] log_lik;
     for (j in 1:N){
       log_lik[j] = poisson_lpmf(Y[j] | mu[j]);
     }
}
"

# Write stan model to file
stan_file <- "./stan/poi_glmm_rand_eff.stan"
writeLines(poi_glm_rand_eff, stan_file)

# Compile stan model
poi_glmm_rand_eff <- cmdstan_model(stan_file)
```

```{r}
split_diverging <- function(fit, var_name) {
    diag_mat <- as.matrix(fit$sampler_diagnostics(format = "matrix"))
    div <- diag_mat[, "divergent__"] == 1
    vals_mat <- as.matrix(fit$draws(var_name, format = "matrix"))
    return(list(vals_mat[div, , drop = FALSE], vals_mat[!div, , drop = FALSE]))
}
```

```{r}
par(mfrow = c(1, 2))

theta_res <- split_diverging(poi_glmm_rand_eff_fit, "theta")
theta_div <- theta_res[[1]]
theta_nondiv <- theta_res[[2]]

sigma_theta_res <- split_diverging(poi_glmm_rand_eff_fit, "sigma_theta")
sigma_theta_div <- sigma_theta_res[[1]]
sigma_theta_nondiv <- sigma_theta_res[[2]]

for (i in 1:2) {
    plot(theta_nondiv[, i], sigma_theta_nondiv[, i], col = "steelblue", log = "y")
    points(theta_div[, i], sigma_theta_div[, i], col = "lightgreen", pch = 19)
}

par(mfrow = c(1, 1))
```

Let's try reparametrizing the model as follows: 

$$
\begin{align*}
    \theta &= \sigma_\theta \cdot \theta_r \\
    \theta_r &\sim \mathcal{N}(0, 1) \\
    \sigma_\theta &\sim HC(0,1)
\end{align*}
$$

```{r message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
poi_glm_rand_eff_reparam <- "
data{
    int<lower = 0> N;
    int<lower = 0> ngr;
    int<lower = 0> nsubgr;
    
    int<lower = 0> p_fix;
    int<lower = 0> p_ran;
    
    array[N] int<lower = 0> Y;
    matrix[N, p_fix] X;
    matrix[N, p_ran] Z;
    
    array[N] int<lower=1, upper=ngr> group;
    array[N] int<lower=1, upper=nsubgr> subgroup;
}

parameters{
    vector[p_fix] beta;            
    vector[ngr] theta_raw;             
    matrix[ngr, p_ran] gamma;      // regression coefficients (random)
    vector[nsubgr] alpha;          // (group specific) random effects
    
    vector<lower=0>[p_fix] sigma_beta;        // variances for the prior on beta
    vector<lower=0>[ngr] sigma_theta;         // variances for the prior on theta
    matrix<lower=0>[ngr, p_ran] sigma_gamma;  // (group specific) random effects
    vector<lower=0>[nsubgr] sigma_alpha;      // (group specific) random effects
}

transformed parameters{
    vector[N] mu;
    vector[N] intercept;
    vector[N] fix_eff;
    vector[N] rand_eff;
    vector[ngr] theta;
    
    theta = sigma_theta .* theta_raw;
    
    intercept = theta[group] + alpha[subgroup];    
    fix_eff = X * beta;
    for (i in 1:N) {
        rand_eff[i] = dot_product(Z[i], gamma[group[i]]);
    }
    
    mu = exp(intercept + fix_eff + rand_eff);  
}

model{
    for (s in 1:N) {
        Y[s] ~ poisson(mu[s]);  
    } 

    for (j in 1:p_fix) {
        beta[j] ~ normal(0.0, sigma_beta[j]);
        sigma_beta[j] ~ cauchy(0, 1);
    }
    
    theta_raw ~ normal(0.0, 1.0);
    sigma_theta ~ cauchy(0, 1);
    
    for (j in 1:nsubgr){
        alpha[j] ~ normal(0.0, sigma_alpha);
        sigma_alpha[j] ~ cauchy(0, 1);
    }
    
    for (j in 1:p_ran) {
      for(i in 1:ngr){
        gamma[j,i] ~ normal(0.0, sigma_gamma[j,i]);
        sigma_gamma[j,i] ~ cauchy(0, 1);
      }
    }
}

generated quantities {
     vector[N] log_lik;
     for (j in 1:N){
           log_lik[j] = poisson_lpmf(Y[j] | mu[j]);
     }
}
"

# Write stan model to file
stan_file <- "./stan/poi_glm_rand_eff_reparam.stan"
writeLines(poi_glm_rand_eff_reparam, stan_file)

# Compile stan model
poi_glmm_rand_eff2 <- cmdstan_model(stan_file)
```

```{r}
poi_glmm_rand_eff_fit <- poi_glmm_rand_eff2$sample(
    data = glmm_randeff_data,
    chains = 4,
    parallel_chains = 4,
    iter_warmup = 1000,
    iter_sampling = 1000,
    refresh = 500
)

poi_glmm_rand_eff_data <- posterior::as_draws(poi_glmm_rand_eff_fit)
```

```{r}
mcmc_trace(poi_glmm_rand_eff_fit$draws(c("beta", "gamma", "theta")))
```

```{r}
par(mfrow = c(1, 2))

theta_res <- split_diverging(poi_glmm_rand_eff_fit, "theta")
theta_div <- theta_res[[1]]
theta_nondiv <- theta_res[[2]]

sigma_theta_res <- split_diverging(poi_glmm_rand_eff_fit, "sigma_theta")
sigma_theta_div <- sigma_theta_res[[1]]
sigma_theta_nondiv <- sigma_theta_res[[2]]

for (i in 1:2) {
    plot(theta_nondiv[, i], sigma_theta_nondiv[, i], col = "steelblue", log = "y")
    points(theta_div[, i], sigma_theta_div[, i], col = "lightgreen", pch = 19)
}

par(mfrow = c(1, 1))
```
